title: Add seq-length bucketing signal (prefill vs decode + effective context) across scheduler -> runtime boundary
creator: Noah Patel
description:
Goal
Add an explicit, low-cardinality sequence-length regime signal for kernel selector v2. This must be available at the scheduler/runtime boundary so the selector can choose different kernels for:
- prefill vs decode
- short vs long effective context (bucketing)

Background / why
Kernel selector v2 needs stable inputs. Today we have a mixture of heuristics spread across runtime codepaths (sometimes derived from request params, sometimes inferred in the kernel wrapper). This produces:
- inconsistent kernel choices for the same workload depending on batching/scheduling
- tail variance when prompt length distribution shifts within a batch
- difficulty correlating kernel selection to latency regressions (missing consistent regime label)

This ticket defines and wires a single source of truth for:
1) phase: PREFILL | DECODE
2) effective context bucket: based on (prompt_len + kv_cache_len) where applicable

Scope
1) Define seq-length bucketing scheme (initial)
- phase: enum {PREFILL, DECODE}
- bucket_id: enum {S0, S1, S2, S3} (names TBD in code, but must be stable and low-cardinality)
- bucket boundaries (initial proposal, can be tuned post-bench):
  - S0: <= 256
  - S1: 257–1024
  - S2: 1025–4096
  - S3: > 4096
Notes:
- We want coarse buckets to avoid telemetry blowups and to keep the selection table manageable.
- Effective context definition differs by phase:
  - Prefill: effective_context = prompt_len (tokens)
  - Decode: effective_context = prompt_len + kv_cache_len (a.k.a. already-decoded tokens) OR an equivalent stable approximation available at scheduling time.

2) Scheduler -> runtime wiring
- Add fields to the internal execution context that is passed from scheduler to runtime:
  - phase (prefill/decode)
  - effective_context_tokens (integer, optional if expensive)
  - seq_bucket (derived enum)
- Ensure the signal works for:
  - streaming and non-streaming
  - micro-batching / continuous batching
  - speculative decode OFF (spec decode is out of scope; if present, must not break)

3) Correctness + determinism constraints
- Must be deterministic for identical request context.
- If any input is unknown, default to a safe bucket/phase such that selector v2 will fall back to safe kernels (per ENG-3923/ENG-3926 behavior). Do not crash or produce high-cardinality labels.

4) Telemetry hooks (minimal)
- Ensure the selection context contains the derived bucket so selector telemetry can log it without re-deriving.
- Do NOT add raw token lengths as labels in metrics.

Acceptance criteria
- Selector v2 receives a non-null phase + seq bucket for >= 99.9% of requests in canary (exceptions: explicitly allowed legacy/edge paths documented).
- Bucket boundaries are unit-tested (including boundary values).
- Observability: traces/events show phase + seq bucket (bucketed, not raw lengths).
- Bench harness can slice results by phase + seq bucket.

Implementation notes / open questions
- Where do we compute kv_cache_len for decode?
  - Prefer: scheduler already tracks per-sequence cache state; expose a stable count.
  - Acceptable fallback: compute from runtime sequence state if scheduler cannot provide it, but keep the value stable across retries.
- For batched requests with mixed prompt lengths:
  - Bucket should be computed per-request/sequence, not per-batch.
  - Runtime selection may still happen at batch-level depending on kernel API; if so, define an aggregation rule (e.g., max bucket) and document it.

Links
- Design doc (context): sources/confluence/eng-serving-runtime/kernel-and-scheduling/kernel-auto-selection-v2-design.json
- Related issues: ENG-3923 (selector v2 core), ENG-3927 (telemetry)
- Related PRs:
  - https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18455 (seq length bucket signal from scheduler)
  - https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18571 (fix seq bucket off-by-one)
  - https://github.com/redwood/redwood/pull/18579 (scheduler instrumentation for prefill/decode split)

Rollout plan (for this change)
- Land behind the selector v2 feature flag (signal should be populated even if v2 disabled, but only used by v2).
- Validate in benchmark-lab by slicing perf by {phase, bucket}.
- Canary: ensure distribution of buckets looks sane vs known prompt distributions; watch for unexpected "unknown" bucket rate.
comments: 2026-01-10 (Lena Fischer): Took this from Noah after design review. Plan: add phase+bucket to SchedulerExecContext, compute bucket per sequence. Need Omar’s sign-off on runtime boundary struct changes.

2026-01-14 (Sofia Ivanova): Scheduler can provide kv_cache_len for decode via existing per-seq state; please avoid recomputing in runtime to keep determinism across retries. Also ensure aggregation rule is documented if selection happens at batch scope.

2026-01-18 (Lena Fischer): Drafted bucket boundaries (<=256, <=1024, <=4096, >4096) to keep table size manageable. Will confirm with Grace/Yuki that these match kernel regime splits they’re using in selection matrix.

2026-01-22 (Grace Kim): Boundaries look OK for first pass. For A10 we’ve seen a cliff around ~2k context, but coarse buckets are fine; we can override per-family later if needed. Please ensure boundary logic is centralized and unit-tested (we’ve been bitten by off-by-one).
2026-01-28 (Lena Fischer): PR up for wiring from scheduler -> runtime context. Added Phase enum and SeqBucket enum. Added fallback to PREFILL+S1 if unknown (so selector v2 will prefer safe kernels).

2026-02-02 (Omar El-Sayed): Reviewed runtime side. One concern: on decode, prompt_len is sometimes 0 in internal continuation requests; please ensure effective_context uses cached length, not prompt_len, or we’ll bucket long-running streams as short decode.
2026-02-05 (Lena Fischer): Fixed decode effective_context to use kv_cache_len + max(prompt_len, 1) for legacy continuation paths. Added unit tests for boundary values and the legacy path.

2026-02-09 (Sana Farid): During canary analysis, bucket distribution looked skewed (S1 vs S2 boundary). Suspect off-by-one at 1024. Please double-check inclusive/exclusive edges and add test at exactly 1024/1025.
2026-02-10 (Lena Fischer): Confirmed bug: boundary used <1024 instead of <=1024. Landed fix + additional tests. Linking follow-up PR (off-by-one fix).
2026-02-14 (Marcus Reed): Perf suite updated to slice by phase+bucket; results now show expected prefill vs decode separation. This unblocked benchmark matrix runs for v2 selector.
2026-02-18 (Lena Fischer): Marking Done. Signal is present in traces and selector context. Next: rely on ENG-3927 to ensure metrics labels stay bucketed (no raw lengths).
